sections.title: Nature, Origin and Basis of International Law

topics.title: Nature, Origin and Basis of International Law

questions.text: Why is it difficult to render accurately a historical account of the origin of International (20) law? What should be the focus of any account as to how and why International law began?

What is International Criminal Law? Describe the composition, basis and jurisdiction (20) of the International Criminal Court (ICC), especially with reference to non-State parties. List all the conditions for the exercise of jurisdiction by the ICC?

(a) What is prescriptive jurisdiction under international law? Examine its (20) various kinds as set out in customary international law. (b) Can a state exercise enforcement jurisdiction in the territory of another state? Discuss by reference to Lotus case (France V. Turkey) 1927.

Describe the role of the states in the enforcement of Public International Law in (20) general. Should the states be entitled to protect their interests directly or should it influence and strengthen the relevant international organs and treaty bodies for this purpose?

topics.title: The Future of International law and Material Sources of International Law

questions.text: What are the material sources of International Law? Discuss any two of them in detail (20) with necessary examples.

sections.title: Relation between International Law and State Law

topics.title: Relation between International Law and State Law

questions.text: “Although Security Council has resolved most of the issues relating to threat to (20) international peace and security but the real problem today is about its composition”. Discuss.

States are considered as original and principal subject of international law. (20) (a) (a) Provide and discuss two examples illustrating the fact that states possess the most full blown form of legal personality under international law. (b) Discuss advantages and disadvantages of the fact that states are still the primary subjects of international law.
Explain the basic difference between Primary and Subsidiary sources of International (20) Law.
Write short notes on any TWO of the following: (10 each) (20) (a) Nature of relationship of a state with an individual. (b) International Soft Law. (c) Collective use of Force.

“From the theoretical stand point, the provision for applying the ‘general principles’ (20) sounding the death ― knell of positivism”. Discuss.

According to Starke, the subject of recognition can be presented, “Less as a body of (20) clearly defined rules or principles than as a body of fluid, inconsistent and unsystematic state practice”. Discuss.
What are the Jurisdictional constraints to the right of self-determination in context to (20) Montevideo Convention on the recognition of state?
What is Recognition? Discuss Dejure and Defacto recognitions. Also explain the (20) constitutive and declaratory theories of recognition. Discuss the disabilities of unrecognized states.

questions.text: To what extent, if at all, are the powers of the Security Council confined to the (20) contents of Chapter VI and VII of the United Nations Charter?

Discuss in detail the structure of the United Nations. Do you believe that the United (20) Nations have the capacity to fulfil the goals of promoting a more united, peaceful and free world? Explain your answer with logical analysis and examples supporting your arguments.
To what extant, if at all, are the powers of the Security Council confined to the contents (20) of Chapters VI and VII of the United Nations Charter?
Elucidate and Justify: “The United Nations, inspite of its imperfections, is the only (20) organization that can save humanity from disaster and complete annihilation”.

topics.title: The International Court of Justice
analysis: Appearances: 3  |  Years: 2021, 2024, 2025  |  Demands: Discuss (1), Evaluate/Assess (1), Explain/Elucidate (1)
Recurring terms: justice (3), court (3), international (3), jurisdiction (2)

questions.text: Explain the structure and powers of the International Court of Justice and assess (20) the importance of the principles laid down in judicial decisions of leading cases as precedents for states.

What is Advisory jurisdiction of International Court of Justice (ICJ)? In what respects (20) it can be distinguished from consent based contentious jurisdiction? Discuss in view of Advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice on the Legal Consequences of the Construction of a Wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory 2004.

Do you think that the International Court of Justice (ICJ) is rightly called the world (20) court? How is the Jurisdiction of the ICJ established? Do you believe that the ICJ should have a more stringent “compulsory jurisdiction” rather than the procedure mentioned in article 36(2) of the ICJ statute?

In the contemporary conflicts, the role of the non-State armed groups has increased as a (20) physical force as well as a political negotiator. Is the current International Law of Armed conflicts equipped enough to deal with the threats posed by the non-State armed groups to the states. Discuss with reference to the right of self defence against these non-State armed groups.

questions.text: Explain the term ‘Subjects of International Law’. Whether States continues to be (20) the principal subjects of international legal relations? Also justify individuals as subject of International Law by giving appropriate examples.

Discuss in detail Recognition in International law and its various kinds. Argue (20) with particular reference to the Constitutive Theory of Recognition and the consequences of non-recognition of government.
Frequent interventions have challenged the validity of some of the fundamental (20) principles of international law. Discuss those principles in light of recent interventions.

(a) Is International law a law or positive morality? Give reasons to support your (20) answer. (b) In what respects, International law differs from domestic law? Are there any similarities between the two?
(a) Narrate the importance of treaty in international law. (20) (b) Explain various steps in conclusion of a treaty.

Consider the role of International Law from the perspective of developing states. A (20) common critique about International Law by the economically weaker states is that it is a product of the practises of the economically developed states, hence protecting the rights of only those states. How do you think the developing states may play a more vibrant role in the development of International Law for the protection of their own interests?
Examine whether article 1 of the 1933 Montevideo Convention on the Rights and (20) Duties of States is an accurate statement of the criteria of statehood in the modern context of International Law.

Explain the laws related with diplomatic immunities under international law. Who is (20) immune and what is the extent of diplomatic immunity? How is Pakistan complying with its responsibilities with regard to the immunity of diplomatic personnel present within its territory?

Distinguish between Monism and Dualism. To what extent both Monism and Dualism (20) explain how States relate to International Law? Critically discuss, ‘Incorporation and Transformation are two modalities for adopting international law into the municipal legal system.
‘A state that first physically occupies a territory retains sovereignty over it forever’. To (20) what extent is this statement true of the acquisition of territory in International Law?

What do you mean by subject of law? Discuss individuals as subjects of International (20) law with special reference to Reparation for injuries suffered in the service of United Nations Organization case 1949.
International Law is Oxymoronic. Argue. (20)
Define International Law. Discuss its nature and scope. To what extent it is relevant (20) and effective in the modern times?
What is meant by “Freedom of High Seas”? Discuss certain restrictions on it by (20) International Law, including the right of Hot Pursuit by the ships of a costal state on the High Seas.
How does International Law deal with POWs? Explain with examples. (20)
